---
title: "Abuse-guard store (Durable Objects)"
description: "Operate the Cloudflare Durable Object store that replaces Upstash Redis for rate limits, clearance, replay fences and password reservations."
---

The `tuturuuu-abuse-guard` Worker (`apps/abuse-guard`) stores short-lived
abuse-protection state in SQLite-backed Durable Objects. It replaces Upstash
Redis for the families listed below. Supabase remains the system of record. The
store holds only losable counters, clearances and fences, and every row has a TTL.

The Worker is **not yet published**. It has no workers.dev URL, preview URLs or
routes. Its first staging and production publication needs owner admission with
the cost and stop evidence from this page.

## Model

| Piece | Role |
| --- | --- |
| `GuardSubject` | One partition. Runs each command batch atomically in one `transactionSync`, so multi-key commands keep the old Lua guarantees. |
| `GuardControl` (`control:v1`) | Durable stop fence and daily operation budget for the whole Worker. |
| `POST /v1/rpc` | HMAC-signed RPC for Vercel-hosted callers. |
| `AbuseGuardEntrypoint.run` | Service-binding RPC for native Workers (Meet, native Calendar). The binding is the trust boundary. |
| `@tuturuuu/utils/abuse-guard/*` | Portable protocol, hashing, clients and backend selection. |

Clients hash every partition and key with `HMAC-SHA256(ABUSE_GUARD_KEY_PEPPER, …)`
before sending. Raw IPs, emails, user or session IDs and tokens never reach
Durable Object names or storage keys. Changing the pepper starts every counter
fresh, so rotate it only with that effect accepted.

### Commands

| Command | Semantics |
| --- | --- |
| `win.hit` | All-or-nothing over up to four sliding (Upstash-weighted) or fixed windows. A denial charges nothing. |
| `kv.get` / `kv.set` (`always`, `nx`, `xx`, `keepTtl`) / `kv.del` / `kv.ttl` / `kv.expire` | TTL records. An expired record reads as absent, which is distinct from a stored zero. |
| `kv.incr` | Integer add. The TTL applies only when the counter is created. |
| `res.reserve` / `res.refund` | Port of the password-attempt Lua: reserve every budget or none, issue a receipt expiring with the target, and refund at most once. |

### Replay safety

Every RPC carries a fresh random operation id inside the signed body. Each
mutating step records `op:<id>:<step>` with its results and a hash of its
commands, in the same transaction as the mutation, for 180 seconds. That covers
the full two-sided ±60-second signature skew, including future timestamps. A
replayed or concurrent duplicate returns the recorded results without charging,
reserving or refunding again. An id reused with different commands is rejected.
Read-only steps record nothing. The Worker verifies the signature over the raw
body and path before parsing JSON.

Clients never retry. A caller that retries a mutating call after an unknown
outcome, such as a timeout, must pass the same `operationId` (from
`createGuardOperationId()`). The retry then returns the original result instead
of charging twice. Unknown names in `ABUSE_GUARD_FAMILIES`, including
wrong-case names, are ignored with a one-time warning. Their family stays on the
legacy path.

### Bounds

One RPC is limited to 16 steps (partitions), 8 commands per step, 32 commands,
4 windows per hit, 16 KiB of body, 2 KiB per value, and a TTL of 1 second to
120 days. The upper TTL covers the 90-day CLI refresh-token replay fence.

### Partitioning

- Generic records, windows, clearance and replay fences get one partition per hashed
  subject key, so there is no hotspot and little storage per object.
- Password, Meet guest and Nova reservations use one partition per limiter scope, so the
  source and target budgets reserve atomically. Throughput is bounded by the caller,
  which runs a password KDF for every admitted attempt.
- A sequential RPC runs its steps in order and skips the rest after the first denial.
  Callers do not rely on snapshot consistency across partitions.

## Selecting the backend

| Variable (Vercel apps) | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `ABUSE_GUARD_FAMILIES` | Comma list from `offline`, `replay`, `proxy`, `password`. **Every family is off by default** and keeps today's legacy (Upstash or missing-store) behavior. |
| `ABUSE_GUARD_URL` | HTTPS origin of the Worker (loopback HTTP only for local verification). |
| `ABUSE_GUARD_SECRET` | Request-signing secret, at least 32 characters. |
| `ABUSE_GUARD_KEY_PEPPER` | Key-hashing pepper, at least 32 characters, separate for each environment. |
| `ABUSE_GUARD_TIMEOUT_MS` | Per-call timeout, default 750, clamped to 100–2000. |
| `ABUSE_GUARD_BACKEND` | Optional: `upstash` forces the legacy path. `off` reports the store as unavailable, so each caller applies its fail policy. |

Once a family is assigned (listed in `ABUSE_GUARD_FAMILIES` or in a native
Worker's injected families), an incomplete or invalid configuration selects
`off`, never the legacy store. A missing or cleartext URL, a missing or short
secret, and a missing or short pepper all count. A fresh legacy store would
forget consumed replay fences and spent limits.

| Variable (Worker) | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `ABUSE_GUARD_SECRETS` | Comma list of accepted signing secrets: current first, then the previous one during rotation. If any entry is shorter than 32 characters, the Worker rejects every RPC with 503. |
| `ABUSE_GUARD_OPERATOR_TOKEN` | Bearer token for `/control/*`, at least 32 characters. It must differ from every signing secret; if it matches one, the Worker rejects every RPC with 503. |
| `ABUSE_GUARD_DAILY_OP_BUDGET` | Total admitted commands per UTC day (default 1,000,000), split across families. |
| `ABUSE_GUARD_FAMILY_BUDGETS` | Optional explicit split, such as `offline=600000,replay=100000`. When empty, offline gets 60%, proxy 20%, and replay and password 10% each. |
| `ABUSE_GUARD_LOCATION_HINT` | Placement hint for new partitions (default `apac`, near Vercel `sin1`). |

Native Workers call `configureAbuseGuardRuntime({ binding: env.ABUSE_GUARD,
pepper, families })` in their adapter instead of the HTTP variables.

Every store failure throws `AbuseGuardUnavailableError`. That includes a timeout,
an auth or configuration error, a stop, and `off`. Once a family is assigned, its
callers fail as follows:

- `offline`: the marked bulk read gets 503.
- `replay`: all three refresh routes fail closed (503). Cross-app session refresh
  always did. CLI refresh and app-token exchange continue on error only while
  `replay` is unassigned.
- `password`: the attempt is refused with `retryAfter: 30`.
- `proxy`: fails open by design. Route limits are skipped, and IP blocks, auth and
  edge controls still apply.

Unassigned families keep their legacy behavior.

## Cost safety

- **Bounds:** the limits above are enforced on the client and again in the Worker
  before any Durable Object call. Each RPC makes at most one subject call per step.
  There are no retries anywhere.
- **Stop fence:** `POST /control/stop` with `Authorization: Bearer
  $ABUSE_GUARD_OPERATOR_TOKEN` persists a stop. Every RPC then returns 503
  `guard_stopped` before any subject call, and stopped requests are not billed.
  Each isolate caches the fence for at most 5 seconds. `POST /control/resume` clears
  it, and `GET /control/state` reads it. Stored data is preserved.
- **Budget:** each family has its own daily allowance, so exhausting one cannot
  stop another. Unauthenticated marked-bulk traffic spends only `offline`'s share.
  Each isolate reports admitted commands per family every 5 seconds or 200
  commands. At 80% of a family's budget the control object logs a warning once.
  When a family exhausts its budget, the control object persists a stop for that
  family only. The stop survives restarts and clears at the next UTC day, so the
  daily cost cap holds without one flood becoming an open-ended outage. The cap
  applies per calendar UTC day, not per rolling 24 hours, so a burst across UTC
  midnight can admit up to about twice a family's budget within a short span. An
  operator resume clears it earlier. Rejected requests are never counted, so a
  family admits its budget plus a bounded overshoot of isolates × 200 commands and
  the 5-second refresh lag. Each caller of a stopped family applies its own fail
  policy.
  An invalid budget configuration makes every RPC return 503
  `guard_unavailable`, the same as a bad secret. That covers a malformed total, an
  unknown or duplicate family, a malformed value, or entries above the total.
- **Alerting:** alert on the `daily operation budget at` warning and the
  `daily operation budget exhausted` error, filtered per family. A stop at
  10:00 GMT+7 lasts until 07:00 GMT+7, the next UTC midnight, unless an operator
  first checks `GET /control/state` and then resumes or stops globally.
- **Alarm failures:** a failed cleanup is logged and re-armed with capped
  exponential backoff (1, 2, 4, 8 minutes). After five consecutive failures it
  stops until the next write; lazy expiry keeps reads correct meanwhile.
- **Alarms:** each partition keeps one alarm at its latest expiry, moved only when
  a write extends it by more than 60 seconds. Cleanup purges at most 1,000 rows per
  wake. An empty partition is wiped with `deleteAll()` and stores nothing. A
  still-warm instance recreates its tables before its next use, and no `abort()`
  is needed. It is never re-armed; otherwise it re-arms
  once at a future expiry. Cleanup makes no network calls, and it logs errors
  instead of throwing so automatic alarm retries cannot loop. Without new writes,
  a partition's alarms end within its longest TTL.
- **Ingress:** when the owner attaches a hostname, add a Cloudflare WAF rate-limit
  rule for it, such as per-IP requests to `/v1/rpc` and `/control/*`. It sheds
  unauthenticated floods before Worker billing. It is not a spend cap; the budget is.
- **Accounting limits:** the budget counts commands, not rows written.
  Each isolate buffers fewer than 200 commands, and those are lost on eviction.
  Stops take up to 5 seconds per isolate to observe. Storage is bounded by
  2 KiB × 120 days × the daily budget. See the
  [adoption guidance](/build/development-tools/oxc-cloudflare-adoption#runaway-work-and-cost-acceptance).

### Pricing envelope

Workers Paid pricing, checked 26 October 2026:

| Service | Included per month | Beyond that |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Base plan | — | $5 |
| Worker requests | 10M | $0.30/M |
| Durable Object requests | 1M | $0.15/M |
| SQLite rows written | 50M | $1.00/M (setAlarm and deletes count) |

Idle Durable Objects are not billed for duration.

| Scenario | Estimate |
| --- | --- |
| Offline guard, one guarded hop | 1 Worker request, 3 Durable Object requests, about 4 rows written |
| One mobile "Download all" (172 reads × 2 hops) | About 1,000 Durable Object requests |
| 1,000 such runs per day | About $5/month above the base |
| Worst case at the default 1M commands/day | About 30M Durable Object requests ($4.35), 60M rows ($10) and 30M Worker requests ($6): **about $20/month above the base, hard-capped by the budget stop** |

The `proxy` family (every API request) has no measured volume and stays off until one exists.

## Local verification

```bash
cd apps/abuse-guard
ttr resources run -- bunx vitest run --maxWorkers=2
```

`src/engine.test.ts` runs the command engine over `node:sqlite` with a
controlled clock. It covers windows, NX/XX semantics, expiry, reservation parity,
cleanup planning and row-write counts. `src/worker.test.ts` bundles the Worker with
esbuild and runs it in workerd through Miniflare. It covers auth rejection with
zero admitted work, secret rotation, a 50-way NX race, clearance expiry,
sequential windows, the service-binding entrypoint, the operator stop fence, and
a budget stop that persists across a restart. Client behavior (timeouts, no
retries, family gating, configuration validation) lives in
`packages/utils/src/abuse-guard/__tests__/`.

Local Durable Objects do not prove hosted placement, latency or billing. Before
production, the admitted staging publication must record each of these:

- p50/p95/p99 latency from `sin1`, measured with a bounded number of RPCs;
- a hosted stop and resume;
- the observed request and row-write counts.

Each non-fair RPC reserves its full command count in GuardControl before subject execution. Reservations survive isolate replacement and are conservatively retained for interrupted or skipped work. Subject operation IDs continue to deduplicate mutations; an unknown transport outcome must not be blindly retried. The restart-before-flush Worker regression verifies that isolate churn cannot exceed the daily allowance.
